# Welcome {.unnumbered}

This is a small site about how I do clinical-epidemiology analysis in R. It is written for students who know a little Stata or a little R and want to see a whole workflow, starting from a messy spreadsheet.

The site grows over time. New chapters are added as the workflow goes further, so check the date at the top for the last update.

Everything runs on one invented trial. Two drugs, A and B, are compared on fasting blood sugar (FBS) at months 0, 3, 6, 9 and 12. Each patient has up to five rows, so the visits of one patient are correlated. All data are simulated and no real patient is involved.

Each chapter takes one script and walks through it step by step. The code you read is loaded straight from the script file, so it is the code that ran. The output sits right under it.

## The pipeline {.unnumbered}

```{mermaid}
%%| echo: false
%%| fig-width: 7
flowchart LR
  A["Simulate<br/>the truth"] --> B["Dirty<br/>Excel sheet"]
  B --> C["Clean<br/>one row per visit"]
  C --> D["Explore<br/>tables and plots"]
  D --> E["Table 1"]
  E -.-> F["Mixed model<br/>(coming)"]
  F -.-> G["more to come"]
  style F stroke-dasharray: 5 5
  style G stroke-dasharray: 5 5
```

| Chapter | Script | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Simulating the trial | `code/0_simulate_data.r` | Writes down the truth and makes the data |
| 2 Cleaning a dirty Excel sheet | `code/1_clean_data.r` | Fixes dates, units, spellings and duplicates |
| 3 Exploring the data | `code/2_basic_explore.r` | Tables and plots, with epicalc and ggplot2 |
| 4 Table 1 with gtsummary | `code/3_table1.r` | A publication style baseline table |
| 5 Plots with ggplot2 | `code/4_ggplot_basics.r` | Basic plots, fitted curves, themes, axes and text, dodging |
| Coming next | | Mixed models for the repeated visits, then more |

## Packages {.unnumbered}

```r
install.packages(c("dplyr", "tidyr", "tibble", "readr", "stringr", "lubridate",
                   "readxl", "janitor", "ggplot2", "rstatix", "gtsummary", "gt",
                   "summarytools", "ragg"))
install.packages("epicalc", repos = "https://medipe.psu.ac.th/epicalc")
```

The epicalc package is no longer on CRAN, so it comes from the repository above.

## How to run it {.unnumbered}

Run each script from the project folder, in this order. The Python line makes the dirty Excel file and needs `openpyxl`.

```sh
Rscript code/0_simulate_data.r
python3 data/_source/make_dirty_fbs.py
Rscript code/1_clean_data.r
Rscript code/2_basic_explore.r
Rscript code/3_table1.r
Rscript code/4_ggplot_basics.r
quarto render
```

Every script is also written to be run in cells, one `#%%@note step N:` block at a time, so you can stop after any step and look at the data.
